subject: Science (Physics)
summary: Exhaustive curriculum coverage of timekeeping and kinematics: historical time measurement devices (sundials, water clepsydras, sand clocks), Galileo Galilei's discovery of pendulum isochronism and oscillatory mechanics (T = 2π√(l/g)), uniform vs non-uniform rectilinear motion, mathematical speed calculations and unit conversions (km/h ↔ m/s), vehicle telemetry (speedometer vs odometer), and analytical interpretation of distance-time graphs.

theory_summary.content: All time measurement relies on natural, repetitive periodic events. 1. Solar Day: Time interval between one sunrise and the next. 2. Lunar Month: Time from one new moon to the next (~29.5 days). 3. Solar Year: Time taken by Earth to complete one full revolution around the Sun (365.25 days). Ancient Timekeeping Devices: (a) Sundials: Measured time by casting shadow of a central angled pointer (gnomon) on a graduated dial plate aligned with Earth's axis (e.g. Maharaja Jai Singh II's massive Samrat Yantra at Jantar Mantar, Jaipur). Ineffective at night or on overcast days. (b) Water Clocks (Clepsydras): Measured time by regulated inflow or outflow of water from calibrated vessels. (c) Sand Hourglasses: Measured fixed intervals by uniform trickle of fine quartz sand through a narrow central neck. Modern Clocks: Regulated by high-frequency piezoelectric vibrations of quartz crystals under an electric field.

A simple pendulum consists of a small, dense metallic sphere (the bob) suspended from a rigid, frictionless support by a light, inextensible thread. Discovered by Galileo Galilei in 1583 inside Pisa Cathedral: 1. Mean Position: The central vertical resting position (O) when the bob hangs at equilibrium. 2. Extreme Positions: The maximum lateral displaced points (A and B) on either side. 3. Amplitude: Maximum displacement of the bob from its mean position to either extreme (OA or OB). 4. One Full Oscillation: Motion of the bob starting from mean O to extreme A, through O to extreme B, and back to O (or from one extreme A to opposite extreme B and back to A). 5. Time Period (T): Time taken by the bob to complete one full oscillation: T = 2π√(l/g). 6. Law of Isochronism: The time period of a simple pendulum depends ONLY on its effective length (l) and the local acceleration due to gravity (g). It is strictly independent of the mass or material of the bob and independent of amplitude for small oscillations.

Motion is a change in the position of an object with respect to time and a chosen reference point. 1. Speed: The total distance covered by an object divided by the total time taken: Speed (v) = Distance (d) / Time (t). 2. Standard Units: Fundamental SI unit of distance is metre (m); time is second (s); SI unit of speed is metre per second (m/s). Practical unit for road/rail vehicles is kilometres per hour (km/h). 3. Golden Kinematic Conversion: To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18 (since 1000 m / 3600 s = 5/18). To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5. Example: 72 km/h = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s. 4. Motion Classification: (a) Uniform Motion: An object travelling along a straight line covering equal distances in equal intervals of time (constant speed). (b) Non-Uniform Motion: Speed changes as the object covers unequal distances in equal time intervals. 5. Vehicle Telemetry: Speedometer records instantaneous speed directly in km/h; Odometer records total cumulative distance travelled in kilometres.

theory_summary.topic: Graphical Kinematics: Distance-Time Graphs & Slope Analysis
theory_summary.content: A Distance-Time graph illustrates the kinematic journey of an object visually: time is plotted on the horizontal x-axis (independent variable) and distance covered is plotted on the vertical y-axis (dependent variable). 1. Stationary / At-Rest Body: Horizontal straight line parallel to the time axis (slope = 0, distance does not change as time advances). 2. Uniform Motion: A straight diagonal line inclined upward at an angle through the origin. 3. Non-Uniform Motion: A curved line (parabolic or fluctuating), indicating changing speed over time. 4. Slope Principle: The slope (gradient) of a distance-time graph represents the speed of the object: Slope = Vertical Change in Distance (Δd) / Horizontal Change in Time (Δt) = Speed (v). A steeper slope signifies greater speed; a flatter slope indicates lower speed.

questions.question: Which of the following device was not used by our ancestors to measure time?
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Quartz clocks utilize modern electronic piezoelectric quartz crystal oscillations, unlike ancient sundials, water clocks (clepsydra), and sand clocks (hourglasses).

questions.question: Which of the following cannot be used for measurement of time?
options: (c) Shadow of an object during the day.
questions.answer: (c) Shadow of an object during the day.
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale A blinking eye is not a regular periodic event and its frequency varies randomly, making it unsuitable for measuring time accurately.

questions.question: How many minutes are there in 6 hours?
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale 1 hour = 60 minutes. Therefore, 6 hours = 6 × 60 = 360 minutes.

questions.question: On Saturday night, Prachi spent 18 minutes on social science homework, 35 minutes on mathematics homework and 22 minutes on english homework. How much time did she spend on her homework?
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Total time spent = 18 min (Social Science) + 40 min (Maths) + 20 min (English) = 78 minutes = 1 hour 18 minutes.

questions.question: How many weeks are there in 56 days?
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale 1 week = 7 days. Number of weeks in 56 days = 56 / 7 = 8 weeks.

questions.question: What part of second is called nanosecond?
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale 1 nanosecond (ns) = 10⁻⁹ second = 1 / 1,000,000,000 of a second (one billionth of a second).

questions.question: How many minutes are there in 4.5 hours?
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale 4.5 hours = 4.5 × 60 = 270 minutes.

questions.question: Two clocks A and B are shown in figure. Clock A has an hour and a minute hand, whereas clock B has an hour hand, minute hand as well as a second hand. Which of the following statement is correct for these clocks? (A) (B)
options: (a) time interval of 30 seconds can be measured by clock A.
(b) time interval of 30 seconds cannot be measured by clock B.
(c) Time interval of 5 minutes can be measured by both A and B.
(d) Time interval of 4 minutes 10 seconds can be measured by clock A. Motion
questions.answer: (a) time interval of 30 seconds can be measured by clock A.
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Clock A (with hour and minute hands) can measure up to 12 hours, while a stopwatch (Clock B) is designed to measure short intervals like seconds and fractions of seconds.

questions.question: How many years are there in a millennium?
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale 1 millennium = 10 centuries = 1000 years.

questions.question: Which of the following does not show periodic motion?
options: (c) Revolution of Earth around the Sun
(d) car moving at a constant speed R
questions.answer: (d) car moving at a constant speed R
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Opening of a door is an irregular, non-periodic event that does not repeat at constant fixed time intervals.

questions.question: Change in position of an object with respect to time is known as
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Motion is defined as the change in position of an object with respect to time and its surroundings.

questions.question: Motion of a car on a straight path is an example of
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Motion of an object in a straight line without changing direction is called rectilinear motion.

questions.question: Which of the following shows a motion in a straight line?
options: (a) Train moving on a straight bridge
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale A train moving on a straight railway track represents rectilinear motion in a straight line.

questions.question: Which of the following is not in uniform motion?
options: (a) bullet travelling with a constant speed in a straight line.
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale A swinging pendulum accelerates as it approaches the mean position and decelerates as it approaches the extreme position, so its speed is continuously changing (non-uniform motion).

questions.question: When a body spins, the body is in
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale When a body turns around an internal fixed axis (spins), it undergoes rotatory motion.

questions.question: Motion of Mars around the Sun is an example of
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Planetary orbits around the Sun repeat at fixed regular intervals of time, making it periodic (and curvilinear/orbital) motion.

questions.question: Which of the following does not show oscillatory motion?
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale A freely falling stone under gravity moves straight downwards in rectilinear accelerated motion, not back-and-forth oscillatory motion.

questions.question: Figure shows an oscillating pendulum. Time taken by the bob to move from A to C is t₁ and from C to O is t₂. The time period of this simple pendulum is
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Time taken from mean position O to extreme position A is T/4. If moving between intermediate points, the time period is determined by harmonic motion relations, confirming option (d).

questions.question: Train A travels with a speed of 80 km/h from Delhi to Chennai. Train B travels from Delhi to Chennai with a speed of 75 km/h. Time and Motion (91 ============================== PAGE 19 ============================== --- COLUMN 1 --- Which of the following statements is true?
options: (a) Trains A and B have same velocity as they are travelling in the same direction.
(b) Trains A and B have same velocity but different speed.
(c) Trains A and B have different speeds and different velocities.
(d) Can't say, the given information is not U enough.
questions.answer: (b) Trains A and B have same velocity but different speed.
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Speed = Distance / Time. If Train A and Train B have the same average speed (80 km/h) over the same route, they will cover equal distances in equal intervals of time.

questions.question: If we denote speed by S, distance by D and time by T, the relationship between these quantities is
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Speed = Distance / Time (S = D / T). Therefore, Distance = Speed × Time (D = S × T) and Time = Distance / Speed (T = D / S).

questions.question: A car travels with speed of 50 km/h in the 1st hour and 100 km/h in the 2nd hour. What the is the total distance covered by the car in two hours?
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Average speed = Total Distance / Total Time. In 1st hour d₁ = 50 km, in 2nd hour d₂ = 100 km. Total distance = 150 km, total time = 2 h. Average speed = 150 / 2 = 75 km/h.

questions.question: Riaz takes 20 min to travel to his school with a speed of 3 m/s. How far is the school?
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Time = 20 min = 20 × 60 = 1200 s. Distance = Speed × Time = 3 m/s × 1200 s = 3600 m = 3.6 km.

questions.question: With what speed should a car travel so that it can cover a distance of 5 km in 5 min?
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Speed = Distance / Time = 500 km / 10 h = 50 km/h.

questions.question: A jet is moving with a speed of 180 km/h. What is its speed in m/s?
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18: 180 × (5/18) = 50 m/s.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to measure the distance travelled by a moving vehicle?
options: (d) Odometer 92 Measurement of Time and Motion --- COLUMN 2 ---
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale An odometer measures and records the total cumulative distance travelled by a vehicle, whereas a speedometer measures instantaneous speed.

questions.question: Which of the following is not matched the correctly?
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Plucking the string of a sitar produces periodic/vibratory motion, not purely rotatory motion.

questions.question: When a body covers equal distance in equal interval of time, it is said to be in
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale When a body covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, its motion is defined as uniform motion.

questions.question: Which one of the following is true for the uniform speed?
options: (a) If speed of the object varies at different interval of time, the object has uniform speed.
(b) If speed of the object is constant at different intervals of time, the object has uniform speed.
(c) If a moving object suddenly comes to rest, the object has uniform speed.
questions.answer: (b) If speed of the object is constant at different intervals of time, the object has uniform speed.
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale A body is said to have uniform speed if it travels equal distances in equal intervals of time, no matter how small these time intervals may be.

questions.question: A cyclist covers 25 km in the first hour, 30 km in the second hour, and 35 km in the third hour. The motion of the cyclist is:
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale The cyclist covers unequal distances (25 km, 30 km, 35 km) in equal intervals of time (1 h each), which represents non-uniform motion.

questions.question: A body is in uniform motion. On which type of path should it travel so that its motion can be called periodic motion?
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale For motion to be completely uniform (constant velocity), both speed and direction must remain constant, which is only possible along a straight path.

questions.question: In a long distance race, the athletes were expected to take four rounds of the track such that the line of finish was same as the line of start. Suppose the length of the track was 200 m. Then what is the displacement of the athletes when they touch the finish line?
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale When an athlete completes full rounds and returns to the exact starting line, the initial and final positions coincide, so the net displacement is zero, even though the distance covered is 4 × perimeter.

questions.question: If a car covers 2/5th of the total distance with speed v₁ and the remaining 3/5th distance with speed v₂, then its average speed for the entire journey is:
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Let total distance be s. Time t₁ = (2s/5)/v₁ = 2s/(5v₁). Time t₂ = (3s/5)/v₂ = 3s/(5v₂). Total time t = s/(5v₁v₂) × (2v₂ + 3v₁). Average speed = s / t = 5v₁v₂ / (3v₁ + 2v₂).

questions.question: A body goes 30 km east then 20 km north then 80 km west and then 50 km east. Find the displacement of the body from the initial position.
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Net East-West displacement = 30 East - 80 West = -50 km (50 km West). Net North-South displacement = 20 North - 50 South = -30 km (30 km South). Magnitude = √(50² + 30²) = √(2500 + 900) = √3400 ≈ 58.3 km (or coordinates (-50, -30)).

questions.question: Boojho walks to his school which is at a distance of 3 km from his home in 30 minutes. On reaching he finds that the school is closed and comes back by a ============================== PAGE 21 ============================== --- COLUMN 1 --- bicycle with his friend and reaches home in 20 minutes. His average speed in km/h is
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Distance to school = 3 km = 3000 m. Time taken = 30 min = 1800 s. Average speed = 3000 / 1800 = 1.67 m/s (or 3 km / 0.5 h = 6 km/h).

questions.question: The speed of a bus is 72 km/h whereas the speed of a car is 12.5 m/s. Which is moving faster?
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Speed of bus = 72 km/h = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s. Speed of car = 12.5 m/s. Since 20 m/s > 12.5 m/s, the bus is moving faster.

questions.question: Which one of the following is an example of uniform motion?
options: (b) An aeroplane flying at a speed of 600 km/h. 94 Measurement of Time and Motion --- COLUMN 2 ---
(c) bee going from one flower to another collecting nectar. cycling in a crowded market.
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale A spacecraft cruising through interstellar space far from gravitational pulls moves with constant speed in a fixed straight line, exemplifying uniform motion.

questions.question: A train travels at 60 km/h for 0.52 h; at 30 km/h for the next 0.24 h and at 70 km/h for the next 0.71 h. What is the average speed of the train?
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Total distance = (60 × 0.52) + (30 × 0.24) + (70 × 0.71) = 31.2 + 7.2 + 49.7 = 88.1 km. Total time = 0.52 + 0.24 + 0.71 = 1.47 h. Average speed = 88.1 / 1.47 ≈ 59.9 km/h (≈ 60 km/h).

questions.question: Train A travels with a speed of 90 km/h from Hyderabad to Bangalore. Train B travels with a speed of 90 km/h from Bangalore to Hyderabad. Which of the following statements is true?
options: (a) Both trains are travelling with the same
(b) Both trains have the same velocity.
(c) Trains A and B have the same speed but different velocities.
(d) Trains A and B have the same velocity but different speeds. An
questions.answer: (a) Both trains are travelling with the same
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Train A speed = 90 km/h. Train B speed = 25 m/s = 25 × (18/5) = 90 km/h. Since both speeds are equal, both trains travel at the exact same speed.

questions.question: The bus decreases its speed from 80 km h-¹ to 60 km h¹ in 5 s. The acceleration of the bus is
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Initial velocity u = 80 km/h = 80 × 5/18 = 22.22 m/s. Final velocity v = 60 km/h = 60 × 5/18 = 16.67 m/s. Acceleration a = (v - u)/t = (16.67 - 22.22)/5 = -5.55 / 5 = -1.11 m/s².

questions.question: A train is travelling from west to east at an average speed of 120 km/h. How far does this train travel in 6.0 second?  ============================== PAGE 22 ============================== --- COLUMN 1 ---
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Distance = 120 km/h × 2.5 h = 300 km eastward.

questions.question: A man walks on a straight road from his home to market 2.5 km away with a speed of 5 km/h. Finding the market closed, he instantly turns and walks back home with a speed of 7.5 km/h. The average speed of the man over the interval of time 0 to 40 min is equal to
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Time to reach market = 2.5 km / 5 km/h = 0.5 h = 30 min. Returning time = 2.5 km / 7.5 km/h = 1/3 h = 20 min. Total time = 50 min. Average speed = Total Distance / Total Time = 5 km / (50/60 h) = 6 km/h.

questions.question: A ship is moving at a speed of 56 km/h. One second later it is moving at 58 km/h. What is its acceleration ?
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Speed change in 1 s = 58 km/h - 56 km/h = 2 km/h = 2 × (5/18) m/s² = 0.55 m/s².

questions.question: The speed of an object can be determined from a graph is called
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale The slope of a distance-time graph (Δdistance / Δtime) gives the speed of the moving object.

questions.question: Look at the following graph. distance time The above graph shows that the object is
options: (d) in uniform acceleration Ap Measurement of Time and Motion 93 Physics  --- COLUMN 2 --- LEVEL-2
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale A straight line parallel to the time axis on a distance-time graph indicates that distance does not change as time passes, meaning the object is stationary (at rest).

questions.question: Look at the following graph carefully and find the velocity of the moving body. 90 80 D i s p l a c e m e n t (m) 70 60 50 40 30 20 10 40 50 50 69 60 330 0 10 20 20 70 Time (s)
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Slope of displacement-time graph gives velocity: v = Δx / Δt = (60 - 0) / (6 - 0) = 10 m/s.

questions.question: When a body is moving with a constant velocity, the displacement time graph will be a
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale For constant velocity, displacement increases linearly with time, so the displacement-time graph is a straight line inclined to the time axis.

questions.question: "When a body is moving with a constant velocity, the velocity-time graph is a straight line parallel to time axis". The given statement
options: (d) none of these speed and same velocity. An
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale When velocity is constant, the velocity-time graph is a horizontal straight line parallel to the time axis.

questions.question: According to the following graph, what happens to the distance covered by the body from 0-10 minutes? Graph of a car Speed moving on a straight road 5 10 Time (in min)
options: (c) It first increases and then decreases.
(d) It first decreases and then increases. JAn
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale A straight line sloping upwards indicates that distance covered increases uniformly as time increases.

questions.question: The velocity-time graph of a body moving in a straight line is shown in the figure. The displacement and distance travelled by the body in 6 s are respectively v (m/s) 5 4 3 2 1 0 23 45 6 Time (s) 1 2 3
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale The area under the velocity-time graph represents the distance travelled. Area of trapezoid/rectangles gives 200 m.

questions.question: The figure shows the displacement-time graph of a particle moving along the x-axis. Which of the following statement will describe the motion of the particle correctly? D i s p l a c e m e n t (m) Time (s)
options: (b) The particle is at rest. Measurement of Time and Motion 95 Physics  --- COLUMN 2 ---
(c) The velocity of the particle increases upto time t₁ and then becomes constant.
(d) The particle moves with a constant velocity upto time t₁ and then stops. An LEVEL 3 - Competency Focused Questions (CFQs)
questions.answer: (c) The velocity of the particle increases upto time t₁ and then becomes constant.
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale The displacement-time graph shows the particle moving in one direction, stopping momentarily at the peak (velocity = 0), and then returning in the opposite direction.

questions.question: The second's hand of a watch is 2 cm long. The speed of the tip of second's hand is
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Radius r = 2 cm = 0.02 m. Time for one complete revolution = 60 s. Speed v = 2πr / T = 2 × 3.1416 × 2 cm / 60 s ≈ 0.209 cm/s ≈ 2.09 × 10⁻³ m/s.

questions.question: A train leaves a station X at 5:00 pm and reaches another station Y at midnight. Its speed is 90 km h-1. What is the distance between X and Y? km
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Departure 5:00 pm, arrival next morning. Total travel time multiplied by average speed gives distance between stations.

questions.question: If the time taken by the bob of a pendulum to move from point R to P is 4 s, then the time taken by it to complete its one oscillation is PO OQ R
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Time period T = 4 × time from mean to extreme = 4 × t = 4t.

options: (a) The object moves with constantly increasing velocity from 0 to P and then it moves with constant velocity.
(b) Velocity of the object increases uniformly.
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale A straight-line distance-time graph sloping upwards indicates uniform speed where distance is directly proportional to time.

questions.question: The distance-time graph of motion of a cycle is shown here. What is the average speed of the cycle over a time period of 12 s ? Distance (m) 0 5 Time (s) 9
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale From the graph, speed = slope = Δdistance / Δtime = (14 - 0) / (7 - 0) = 2 m/s.

questions.question: A train moving on linear path travels a distance D at a constant speed of 30 km/h, then it travels the same distance in opposite direction and reaches initial position at a constant speed of 45 km/h. What is the average speed of the train?
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Time taken t₁ = D / v₁, return time t₂ = D / v₂. Average speed = 2D / (t₁ + t₂) = 2v₁v₂ / (v₁ + v₂).

questions.question: Rohan is going to school with his father by car. He decides to note the readings on the odometer of the car after every five minutes till he reaches the school. The given table shows the odometer readings of his journey. Time (a.m.) 7:30 7:35 7:40 7:45 7:50 Odometer 36593 36596 36599 36602 36605 reading (km) If he left for school at 7:30 am, then find the average speed of the car.
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Rohan's odometer readings give the distance travelled in the recorded time intervals, enabling calculation of average speed in km/h and m/s.

questions.question: Read the given statements and select the correct option. Statement 1: Circular motion is the motion along a curve traced out by a moving object such that its distance from a fixed point is constant. Statement 2: The motion of a wheel of a moving bicycle is same as the motion of a mark on the blades of a moving electric fan.
options: (a) Both statements 1 and 2 are true and statement 2 is the correct explanation of statement 1.
(b) Both statements 1 and 2 are true but statement 2 is not the correct explanation of statement 1. Measurement of Time and Motion 96 --- COLUMN 2 ---
(c) Statement 1 is true but statement 2 i false.
(d) Statement 1 is false but statement 2 is true.
questions.answer: (b) Both statements 1 and 2 are true but statement 2 is not the correct explanation of statement 1. Measurement of Time and Motion 96 --- COLUMN 2 ---
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Statement 1 is true (instantaneous speed can be positive while average velocity is zero for closed loops). Statement 2 is also valid.

questions.question: A person is running along a circular track of area 625 π m² (л = 22/7) with a constant speed. Find the displacement in 15 seconds if he has to complete the race in 30 seconds.
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Area = πr² = 625π m² ⇒ r² = 625 ⇒ r = 25 m. Diameter = 2r = 50 m. For a semi-circle, distance = πr = 25π m, and displacement = diameter = 50 m.

questions.question: Distance-time graph of an object is shown in the figure. Object is at rest in a time interval from Distance T RS 0\10 11 12 13 14 Time
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale The object is at rest in the time interval where the distance remains horizontal and constant (slope = 0), between t₂ and t₃.

questions.question: A car covers 30 km at a uniform speed of 60 km/h and the next 30 km at a uniform speed of 40 km/h. The total time taken is
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Time for first 30 km = 30 / 60 = 0.5 h = 30 min. Time for next 30 km = 30 / 40 = 0.75 h = 45 min. Total time = 30 + 45 = 75 minutes. Average speed = 60 km / 1.25 h = 48 km/h.

questions.question: An athlete completes one round of a circular track of radius R in 40 seconds. The displacement at the end of 2 minute 20 second will be
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Total time = 2 min 20 s = 140 s. Number of rounds = 140 / 40 = 3.5 rounds. After 3 full rounds, the athlete is at the start; after the additional 0.5 round, the athlete is at the diametrically opposite point. Net displacement = diameter = 2R.

questions.question: In a 200 m race, two competitors P and reached the finishing line at the same time. Which of the following graphs shows that both the competitors reached the finishing line at time t? Speed (ms¹) Speed (m s¯¹) Q
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Both competitors covered the same distance (200 m) in the same total time, so their average speeds were identical.

questions.question: Parsec is the unit of
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Parsec (parallax second) is an astronomical unit of length/distance used to measure distances to stars (1 parsec ≈ 3.26 light-years ≈ 3.086 × 10¹⁶ m).

questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale Speed is 2 m/s during the time interval where slope = 2 m/s. Slope between t = 3s and t = 6s is (12 - 6) / (6 - 3) = 6 / 3 = 2 m/s, so at t = 5.0 s.

questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s ≈ 0.2778 m/s, not 18/5 m/s.

(b) The car is slowest in between 10 and 20 seconds.

questions.answer: (b) The car is slowest in between 10 and 20 seconds.

questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale A speed-time graph cannot have multiple values of speed at the same instant of time (vertical line), nor can speed be negative.

questions.question: A speed-time (v-t) graph of an object is shown where speed increases from zero, curves, and asymptotically flattens horizontally. Which of the following best describes the motion?
options: (a) The object is thrown upwards through vacuum.
(b) The object is dropped downwards through air and reaches terminal velocity.
(c) The object is thrown downwards through vacuum with constant acceleration.
(d) The object is undergoing uniform circular motion.
questions.answer: (b) The object is dropped downwards through air and reaches terminal velocity.
questions.explanation: Scientific & Mathematical Rationale An object falling through air starts from zero speed, accelerates under gravity, and experiences air drag proportional to speed until drag balances weight, approaching constant terminal velocity (asymptotic curve).

questions.question: Periodic motion _______ is a motion in which a body repeats the motion at equal intervals of time.
questions.explanation: Explanation Correct Answer: periodic. Repeats at fixed time periods.

questions.question: The device used in vehicles to measure the speed is called a/an _______ .
questions.explanation: Explanation Correct Answer: speedometer. Measures instantaneous speed in km/h.

questions.question: The basic SI unit of speed is _______ .
questions.explanation: Explanation Correct Answer: m/s. Metre per second is the base SI unit.

questions.question: The time taken by a pendulum to complete one full oscillation is called its _______ .
questions.explanation: Explanation Correct Answer: time period. Denoted by T and measured in seconds.

questions.question: In a distance-time graph, a straight line inclined to the time axis indicates _______ motion.
questions.explanation: Explanation Correct Answer: uniform. Equal distance in equal intervals of time.

questions.question: The distance-time graph of an object at rest is a straight line _______ to the time axis.
questions.explanation: Explanation Correct Answer: parallel. Zero slope means zero speed.

questions.question: The metallic ball of a simple pendulum is called its _______ .
questions.explanation: Explanation Correct Answer: bob. Suspended by a light inextensible string.

questions.question: A car travels at 36 km/h. Its speed expressed in m/s is _______ m/s.
questions.explanation: Explanation Correct Answer: 10. 36 * (5/18) = 10 m/s.

questions.question: One microsecond is equal to _______ part of a second.
questions.explanation: Explanation Correct Answer: one millionth. 10^-6 seconds = 1 microsecond.

questions.question: The slope of a distance-time graph represents the _______ of the moving body.
questions.explanation: Explanation Correct Answer: speed. Slope = Delta(Distance) / Delta(Time) = Speed.

questions.question: The basic unit of time is second (s).
questions.explanation: Explanation True. Second is the fundamental SI unit of time across the globe.

questions.question: Every object moves with a constant speed.
questions.explanation: Explanation False. Most real-world motions are non-uniform with variable speed.

questions.question: Distances between two cities are measured in kilometres.
questions.explanation: Explanation True. Kilometres (km) is the standard practical unit for long geographical distances.

questions.question: The time period of a given pendulum is not constant.
questions.explanation: Explanation False. Galileo proved that for a pendulum of fixed length, the time period remains remarkably constant.

questions.question: The speed of a train is expressed in m/h.
questions.explanation: Explanation False. Train speed is expressed in km/h or m/s, never in metres per hour.

questions.question: The distance-time graph for the motion of an object moving with a constant speed is a straight line.
questions.explanation: Explanation True. Constant slope directly represents constant speed.

questions.question: A sundial can measure time accurately during rainy or cloudy days.
questions.explanation: Explanation False. Sundials require clear sunlight to cast a distinct shadow on the dial.

questions.question: The motion of a spinning top is an example of rectilinear motion.
questions.explanation: Explanation False. A spinning top executes rotatory (rotational) motion around a central axis.

questions.question: A nanosecond is one billionth of a second.
questions.explanation: Explanation True. 1 nanosecond = 10^-9 s = 1/1,000,000,000 second.

questions.question: Speedometer measures the total distance travelled by a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Explanation False. The speedometer measures instantaneous speed, while the odometer measures distance.

questions.question: Give the name of the device which measures the distance covered by a vehicle.
questions.answer: An Odometer measures and records the total cumulative distance travelled by a vehicle in kilometres.
questions.explanation: Official textbook model solution and marking rubric breakdown.

questions.question: Why could sundials not be used as universal timekeepers around the clock?
questions.answer: Sundials rely on the casting of shadows by sunlight on a calibrated gnomon dial. Therefore, they cannot measure time at night, during cloudy or overcast weather, or indoors.
questions.explanation: Official textbook model solution and marking rubric breakdown.

questions.question: Define a Solar Day and a Lunar Month.
questions.answer: Solar Day: The time interval between one sunrise and the consecutive next sunrise.Lunar Month: The time interval from one new moon phase to the very next new moon phase (approx. 29.5 days).
questions.explanation: Official textbook model solution and marking rubric breakdown.

questions.question: On what scientific principle are modern wristwatches and quartz clocks based?
questions.answer: Modern quartz clocks and watches work on the principle of the high-frequency periodic vibrations of a tiny quartz crystal driven by a miniature electric cell, offering extremely precise and stable timekeeping.
questions.explanation: Official textbook model solution and marking rubric breakdown.

questions.question: Give the term used for the time taken by a pendulum to complete one oscillation.
questions.answer: It is termed as the Time Period ($T$) of the pendulum.
questions.explanation: Official textbook model solution and marking rubric breakdown.

questions.question: Explain Galileo's discovery regarding the simple pendulum at Pisa Cathedral.
questions.answer: In 1583, Galileo Galilei observed a swinging chandelier in Pisa Cathedral and timed the oscillations against his own pulse. He discovered that a pendulum of a given length always takes the exact same time to complete one swing, regardless of amplitude. This property is known as isochronism and laid the foundation for pendulum clocks.
questions.explanation: Official textbook model solution and marking rubric breakdown.

questions.question: A simple pendulum takes 32 s to complete 20 oscillations. Calculate its time period and frequency.
questions.answer: Time Period: $T = \frac{\text{Total Time Taken}}{\text{Number of Oscillations}} = \frac{32\text{ s}}{20} = 1.6\text{ s}$.Frequency: $f = \frac{1}{T} = \frac{1}{1.6} = 0.625\text{ Hz}$ (or oscillations per second).
questions.explanation: Official textbook model solution and marking rubric breakdown.

questions.question: State the factors that affect the time period of a simple pendulum and two factors that do NOT affect it.
questions.answer: Factors that affect Time Period: (1) Effective length of pendulum ($T \propto \sqrt{L}$), (2) Acceleration due to gravity ($g$).Factors that DO NOT affect Time Period: (1) Mass or material of the bob, (2) Amplitude of swing (for small angular displacements < 15°).
questions.explanation: Official textbook model solution and marking rubric breakdown.

questions.question: Define Speed. Write its formula and SI unit.
questions.answer: Speed is defined as the distance travelled by an object per unit of time: $$\text{Speed} = \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Time}}$$. Its SI unit is metre per second (m/s).
questions.explanation: Official textbook model solution and marking rubric breakdown.

questions.question: Convert 54 km/h into m/s and 25 m/s into km/h.
questions.explanation: Official textbook model solution and marking rubric breakdown.

questions.question: Distinguish clearly between Distance and Displacement.
questions.answer: DistanceDisplacementTotal path length covered (Scalar).Shortest straight-line distance from start to end (Vector).Always positive ($d > 0$ for moving bodies).Can be positive, negative, or zero.Does not decrease with time.Can decrease if body returns towards start.

questions.question: The distance between two stations is 240 km. A train takes 4 hours to cover this distance. Calculate the speed of the train in km/h and m/s.
questions.answer: $\text{Speed in km/h} = \frac{240\text{ km}}{4\text{ h}} = 60\text{ km/h}$.$\text{Speed in m/s} = 60 \times \frac{5}{18} = 16.67\text{ m/s}$.
questions.explanation: Official textbook model solution and marking rubric breakdown.

questions.question: The odometer of a car reads 57321.0 km at 08:30 AM. At 08:50 AM, the odometer reads 57336.0 km. Find speed in km/min and km/h.
questions.answer: Distance covered $\Delta s = 57336.0 - 57321.0 = 15.0\text{ km}$.Time taken $\Delta t = 20\text{ min} = \frac{1}{3}\text{ h}$.$\text{Speed in km/min} = \frac{15\text{ km}}{20\text{ min}} = 0.75\text{ km/min}$.$\text{Speed in km/h} = \frac{15\text{ km}}{1/3\text{ h}} = 45\text{ km/h}$.
questions.explanation: Official textbook model solution and marking rubric breakdown.

questions.question: What is the shape of distance-time graph for a body moving with uniform speed?
questions.answer: A straight line inclined to the time axis. The constant slope directly represents the constant speed.
questions.explanation: Official textbook model solution and marking rubric breakdown.

questions.question: How does a distance-time graph show that a body is at rest?
questions.answer: When a body is at rest (stationary), its distance from the origin does not change as time elapses. Hence, the graph is a horizontal straight line parallel to the time axis (Slope = 0).
questions.explanation: Official textbook model solution and marking rubric breakdown.

questions.question: Interpret the physical meaning of the slope of a Distance-Time graph.
questions.answer: The slope (gradient) of a Distance-Time graph is given by: $$\text{Slope} = \frac{\Delta y}{\Delta x} = \frac{\text{Change in Distance}}{\text{Change in Time}} = \text{Speed}$$. A steeper slope represents higher speed.
questions.explanation: Official textbook model solution and marking rubric breakdown.

questions.question: standard textbook Q1: Calculate speed of car that travels 150 metres in 10 seconds. Express answer in km/h.
questions.answer: Speed in m/s = $\frac{150\text{ m}}{10\text{ s}} = 15\text{ m/s}$.Speed in km/h = $15 \times \frac{18}{5} = 54\text{ km/h}$.
questions.explanation: Official textbook model solution and marking rubric breakdown.

questions.question: standard textbook Q2: A train travels 180 km in 3 hours. Find its speed in (i) km/h, (ii) m/s, and (iii) distance covered in 4 hours at constant speed.
questions.answer: (i) Speed in km/h = $\frac{180}{3} = 60\text{ km/h}$.(ii) Speed in m/s = $60 \times \frac{5}{18} = 16.67\text{ m/s}$.(iii) Distance in 4 hours = $60\text{ km/h} \times 4\text{ h} = 240\text{ km}$.
questions.explanation: Official textbook model solution and marking rubric breakdown.

questions.question: HOTS Q3: A vehicle travels along a straight line covering 2 km. First 500 m at 10 m/s, next 500 m at 5 m/s. What speed is needed for the remaining 1000 m so that total journey takes 200 s? What is average speed?
questions.answer: Total distance $s = 2000\text{ m}$, Total time $t = 200\text{ s}$.Time for first 500 m: $t_1 = \frac{500}{10} = 50\text{ s}$.Time for second 500 m: $t_2 = \frac{500}{5} = 100\text{ s}$.Remaining time available: $t_3 = 200 - (50 + 100) = 50\text{ s}$.Remaining distance: $2000 - 1000 = 1000\text{ m}$.Required speed $v_3 = \frac{1000\text{ m}}{50\text{ s}} = 20\text{ m/s}$.Average speed = $\frac{2000\text{ m}}{200\text{ s}} = 10\text{ m/s}$ (or $36\text{ km/h}$).
questions.explanation: Official textbook model solution and marking rubric breakdown.

questions.question: HOTS Q4: A car covers 30 km at a uniform speed of 60 km/h and the next 30 km at a uniform speed of 30 km/h. Find the average speed of the car for the complete 60 km trip.
questions.answer: Total distance $d = 30 + 30 = 60\text{ km}$.Time for first part: $t_1 = \frac{30\text{ km}}{60\text{ km/h}} = 0.5\text{ h} = 30\text{ min}$.Time for second part: $t_2 = \frac{30\text{ km}}{30\text{ km/h}} = 1.0\text{ h} = 60\text{ min}$.Total time $t = t_1 + t_2 = 1.5\text{ h}$.$$\text{Average Speed} = \frac{\text{Total Distance}}{\text{Total Time}} = \frac{60\text{ km}}{1.5\text{ h}} = 40\text{ km/h}$$.Note: Common student trap is taking the arithmetic mean $(60 + 30)/2 = 45\text{ km/h}$, which is incorrect because time spent at each speed is different!
questions.explanation: Official textbook model solution and marking rubric breakdown.
